correctness.rationale: The symmetric cubic difference is 3τt²+τ³/4. With kernel exp(−2πiνt), the quadratic coefficient is 2π(1−i(3λ/(2π))τ), whose real part is positive. The complex Gaussian formula gives a nowhere-zero amplitude with modulus exp(−πτ²/2)(1+c²τ²)^(−1/4)exp(−πν²/[2(1+c²τ²)]). Doppler integration at fixed τ gives the correctly normalized moment integral; its Gaussian tail controls every finite c and p>0. The sign of (2−p)/4 proves strict monotonicity off p=2 and M₂=1. Setting s=c²τ² on the two half-lines gives the stated Tricomi parameters and Γ(1/2) prefactor. For p<4 the divided integrand is dominated by a Gaussian times (1+τ²)^((2−p)/4) when p≤2, or by the Gaussian times |τ|^(1−p/2) when 2<p<4. Its integral gives K_p. For p>4 the rescaled cτ integrand has integrable limiting power 1−p/2 and its beta integral gives D_p. At p=4 set cτ=sinh(v); the doubled half-line integral with cosh(2v) yields e^(π/c²) K₀(π/c²)/(√2 c). Expansion of K₀ with the exponential prefactor gives the displayed constant and O(log(c)/c³). Independent 40-decimal quadrature in the v-coordinate at c=30,300,3000 gave 0.136561316293361361, 0.0244638413705885238, 0.00353174899797265098 respectively, with deviations from the two-term expression approximately 4.76×10⁻⁴, 8.54×10⁻⁷, 1.23×10⁻⁹. The asymptotic proof is analytic and fixed-p, not an inference from these samples.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the full fixed-exponent moment law of the continuous Gaussian-envelope cubic chirp together with the three-regime strong-chirp behavior and critical constant. Gaussian integration, Moyal normalization, Lieb's endpoint and the special-function identities are standard. Comparisons with previously treated zero sets, cubic-chirp parameter analysis and discrete moment formulas do not establish the same continuum law. This is a bounded evidence judgment, not a claim of absolute priority for zero-free examples or the pointwise Gaussian integral.

value.rationale: The L^p moment is motivated by sharp ambiguity bounds, and a normalized Gaussian with cubic phase gives a natural one-parameter deformation. The complete fixed-order law captures a nontrivial integrability threshold and exact rates (including a critical logarithm) invisible to the universal bound, even though pointwise zero-freeness and the Moyal normalization persist. This is more than a sample quadrature or a re-expression of the endpoint inequality.
residual_risks: The result is a specific analytic model; no general signal or application theorem is inferred.
